title: Evaluation study of the therapy program TraFiK – training of final consonants in children with sensorineural hearing impairment
summary:
Based on previous findings on the language acquisition of children with a sensorineural hearing impairment, the therapy program "TraFiK – training of final consonants" was developed for speech therapy practice. The therapy program focusses on training the perception, discrimination and production of word-final consonants, particularly the consonants /s/, /t/, /n/ and the consonant cluster /st/. These consonants are crucial for grammatical language development because they can carry grammatical information, as is the case for verb endings that mark agreement with the subject (e.g. "du gehst" (you go) or "sie geht" (she goes)). The therapy program "TraFiK" aims at training the perception, discrimination and production of these consonants in syllable-final, word-final and verb-final position. 
The evaluation study will compare the effectiveness and handling of the "TraFiK" program against the effectiveness of speech therapy commonly supplied to children with a hearing-impairment. 
Study participants are children aged 4-6 years with a bilateral hearing impairment who are fitted with hearing aids and/or CI, who communicate in spoken German, who receive speech therapy and who have no other developmental disorders. The children are tested with respect to their ability to discriminate and produce the critical consonants in word-final position as well as in inflected verbs before and after a 3-months therapy phase. During the therapy phase, either the already ongoing speech therapy is continued as usual or therapy is provided according to the new therapy program "TraFiK".

This group includes children who meet the inclusion criteria and were assigned to the study group according to the criteria for parallelization. They receive speech and language therapy according to the new therapy program "TraFiK". The children's therapists are trained in advance for this purpose.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- diagnosed bilateral, sensorineural hearing impairment,
- supplied with CIs and/or hearing aids,
- communicating in spoken German/ child grows up in a German-speaking environment,
- regular attendance of speech therapy,
- normal non-verbal IQ, measured by the SON-R at the first time point of testing (Tellegen & Laros, 2007),
- no other developmental disorders (mental, psycho-social)
Exclusion criteria:
- additional developmental disorders (see above),
- nonverbal-mental IQ below 80,
- less than 24 months of contact with German
